newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sees wheat prices falling on EU harvest.
newsitem.headline: Manila sees wheat prices falling on EU harvest.

text.p: Philippine flour mills are standing back from the market on hopes that U.S. wheat prices will soften further in the coming week due to a bumper crop in the European Union, traders said on Friday.

"Prospects for U.S. wheat prices to slide some more are promising as the European Union started to give subsidy to its wheat buyers this week due to better harvests among its members," said an executive at one of Manila's largest millers.
Philippine flour millers stayed away from the market this week due to ample local supplies and despite a sharp fall in U.S. grains prices on Wednesday.

U.S. analyst Vic Lespinasse at Dean Witter Reyolds on Wednesday cited reports of improved harvests around the globe, which may replenish world grain stocks that are at their lowest in 20 years, as a factor contributing to the retreat in prices.
Philippine traders said that unless there is a substantial further reduction in U.S. wheat prices, local buyers will continue to be sidelined.
Some local flour millers still have enough supply for the next two months so they can bide their time, one trader said.
The Department of Trade and Industry said the prevailing retail price of hard flour, which is used in making bread, in Metro Manila was steady at 315 pesos ($12.11) per 25 kg.
The prevailing retail price of soft flour, which is used in making cakes and pastries, also remained wedged at 275 pesos ($10.57) per 25 kg.
On Friday, Philippine traders and industry executives said that local hog raisers planned to buy 150,000 tonnes of corn in the fourth quarter.
"We have asked the (state-owned) National Food Authority (NFA) to import for us," said an industry executive.
On Tuesday, feed millers said they had asked the NFA to import for them another 150,000 tonnes corn in anticipation of the lean months in the first quarter of 1997.
The private sector usually asks the NFA to import grains for them in order to obtain lower tariffs.
Domestic Philippine corn prices were mixed this week.

The NFA said the average retail price of yellow corn jumped to 10.24 pesos (39.38 U.S. cents) per kg from the previous week's 10.18 pesos (39.15 cents), while the average retail price of white corn dropped to 10.60 pesos (40.76 cents) per kg from 11.45 pesos (44 cents).
